title: Held beyond legal limits? Lawyers seek dismissal of ASEAN protest raps
summary: The National Union of Peoples' Lawyers has filed motions seeking the dismissal of complaints against protesters.

blocks.text: Protesters clash with police officers during a demonstration that coincides with the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Leaders' Summit and Related Summits in Manila on Nov. 15, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — The National Union of Peoples' Lawyers (NUPL) has asked prosecutors to dismiss complaints against protesters arrested during the ASEAN summit, arguing that they were detained beyond the period allowed by law and denied their right to the speedy disposition of cases.

NUPL chair Edre Olalia told Philstar.com that the group filed the motions before the Muntinlupa City Prosecutor's Office on behalf of protesters arrested in Sucat, Muntinlupa City, on Sunday, November 15.

Olalia said the motions were based on the protesters' continued detention beyond the maximum allowed period without the timely filing of complaints, as well as alleged violations of their right to the speedy disposition of cases.
He also confirmed that law enforcement officers had asked protesters whether they wanted to waive their rights under Article 125 of the Revised Penal Code, describing such inquiries as "routinary."
Article 125 sets the time limits for bringing people arrested without a warrant before the proper judicial authorities.
The law provides detention limits of 12 hours for offenses punishable by light penalties, 18 hours for correctional penalties and 36 hours for afflictive or capital penalties.
A detainee may waive these limits to undergo a preliminary investigation instead of an immediate inquest. Such a waiver must be voluntary and executed with the assistance of legal counsel.
More than 200 protesters were arrested in separate demonstrations across Metro Manila on Nov. 15, as Southeast Asian leaders gathered in the Philippines for the 49th ASEAN Summit.

According to a STAR report, protesters arrested in Muntinlupa, mostly members of Lakbayan ng Timog Katagalugan, underwent inquest proceedings over alleged violations of Batas Pambansa 880, or the Public Assembly Act, as well as alarm and scandal, and resistance and disobedience to persons in authority.
Nine protesters faced additional complaints for grave coercion and malicious mischief over allegations that they broke into a convenience store and damaged property.

Meanwhile, eight activists arrested at Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila underwent separate inquest proceedings for alleged tumult and other disturbances of public order, direct assault and illegal assembly.
The motions filed by NUPL concern the protesters arrested in Muntinlupa.
The filing of criminal complaints before prosecutors does not necessarily mean charges have been filed in court.
